title: Expositio Fidei
author: Monumenta Vetera Ad Arianorum Doctrinam
source: Translated by Claude from tmp207.tmp207.opp-lat1, as held by Open Greek and Latin's Patrologia Latina.

passages.original: unius tamen deitatis, unius essentia, uniusque Substantiae, in tribus quidem subsistentiis seu personis, ut Pater pater sit, Filius filius sit, Spiritus sanctus spiritus sanctos sit, in una natura onaque substantia, ut Deos unus et solus et summus credatur. Non tres naturas introducentes ut Arius blasphemat, qui tres deos praedicavit, excellentiorem, minorem, et infe- riorem. Nos vero sanctam Trinitatem in unitate, et unitatem in sancta Trinitate confitemur. Nam cum dicimus omnipotentem Patrem, appellatio hujus Paterni nominis ad Filii personam attenditur.
passages.english: yet of one deity, of one essence, and of one substance, in three subsistences, that is, persons, so that the Father is father, the Son is son, the Holy Spirit is holy spirit, in one nature and one substance, so that God is believed [to be] one and alone and supreme. [We do] not introduce three natures, as Arius blasphemes, who preached three gods: a more excellent, a lesser, and a lower. We, however, confess the holy Trinity in unity, and unity in the holy Trinity. For when we say "the almighty Father," the designation of this paternal name is directed to the person of the Son.
passages.notes: Scanning errors corrected: "sanctos" for "sanctus", "onaque" for "unaque", "Deos" for "Deus", "infe- riorem" for "inferiorem". "Essentia" (for "essentiae") is read as genitive in line with the parallel phrases.
